language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_EDITMENU1: You are now in the Edit Menu.^Now that you have selected a Clip to Edit, you need to choose what kind of Edit you want to do.^Remember, you can only apply one Camera to a Clip, but you can do multiple effects.^Cameras let you set up cool camera angles. How they track and follow your skater depends on which Camera you choose.^Follow Camera: Always follows and points at your skater.^(Continued on Next Page)
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_EDITMENU2: Tripod Camera: Remains stationary while always pointing at your skater.^Game Camera: As its name implies, this is the normal view you see in gameplay.^Effects let you set the speed of the Clip and apply a variety of effects to make the Clip look unique.^Lastly, the advanced versions of each camera will allow you to transition the camera smoothly between multiple positions within your Clip, instead of cutting directly to each new camera position.
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_FOLLOWCAMERA: You are now in the Clip Editing Mode for Follow Camera.^^This Camera always points at and follows your skater. You can set the angle, distance, zoom, and where on the skater's body the camera is pointing.
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_FOLLOWCAMERA_A: You are now in the Clip Editing Mode for Advanced Follow Camera.^This Camera is just like the regular Follow Camera, except now you can set Keys!^^Advanced Cameras: In the regular Camera modes, you could make your Camera do 1 thing per Clip. With the Advanced Cameras you can make your Camera smoothly transition between multiple angles and positions all in one Clip. You do this by placing Key Markers.^^(Continued on Next Page)

Key Markers: These are points in the action where you want your Camera to do something. When you place a Key Marker, you set the properties of the Camera just like you did with the regular Cameras. When you do this with a bunch of keys in one Clip, the Camera will animate smoothly between the properties of each Key Marker!
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_FREECAMERA: You are now in the Clip Editing Mode for Free Camera.^^This is a stationary Camera that you can point at anything you want! You set the angle, position, and zoom.^Remember that the Free Camera can only be a certain distance away from your skater. If your skater gets too far away, the Free Camera will switch to Game Camera.
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_FREECAMERA_ADV: You are now in the Clip Editing Mode for Advanced Free Camera.^This Camera is just like the regular Free Camera, except now you can set Keys!^Advanced Cameras: In the regular Camera modes, you could make your Camera do 1 thing per Clip. With the Advanced Cameras you can make your Camera smoothly transition between multiple angles and positions all in one Clip. You do this by placing Key Markers.^(Continued on Next Page)

Key Markers: These are points in the action where you want your Camera to do something. When you place a Key Marker, you set the properties of the Camera just like you did with the regular Cameras. When you do this with a bunch of keys in one Clip, the Camera will animate smoothly between the properties of each Key Marker!
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_GAMECAMERA: You are now in the Clip Editing Mode for the Game Camera. This is pretty much the same as the game camera you see when playing the game but here you can adjust the zoom.
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_INSTANTREPLAY1: You are now in Instant Replay Mode.^Whenever you do something awesome, use this mode to see it again in detail! If you like what you see, you can take a Snapshot or even make a Video to keep or share with your buddies!^(Continued on Next Page)
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_INSTANTREPLAY2: Timeline: It's that strip along the top of the screen. The right side is where you paused the game. The left side is how far back in time you can go.^Scrub: It's what you do when you move that little cursor (or Scrub Tool) back and forth across the timeline.
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_MAINTIMELINE1: You are now in Main Timeline Edit Mode.^This is your first and last stop for editing videos!^The Editing Cycle:^1) Start at the Main Timeline, set the length, and divide it into Clips.^2) Choose a Clip, edit it, return to the Main Timeline, choose another Clip to edit, and so on.^3) When you are done, the Main Timeline Edit Mode is where you decide to save, share, or discard your video.^In and Out Points: The first thing you want to do is figure out where your Video starts and ends. You do this by setting your In Point (Start) and Out Point (End).^Time: This shows the total length of time of your video between the In and Out Points.^(Continued on Next Page)
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_MAINTIMELINE2: Clip Markers: You can make your Video switch between a bunch of cool Camera angles and effects. To do this you divide the Timeline into Clips by placing Clip Markers. Then you can customize a Clip by Scrubbing over it and Editing it. If you don't want to place any Clip Markers, then just think of the Timeline as being one big Clip.^^Timeline: It's that strip along the top of the screen. The right side is where you paused the game. The left side is how far back in time you can go.^^Scrub: It's what you do when you move that little cursor (or Scrub Tool) back and forth across the Timeline.
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_TRIPODCAMERA: You are now in the Clip Editing Mode for Tripod Camera.^^This Camera always points at your skater but remains in one spot. You can set the angle, position, zoom, and where on the skater's body the camera is pointing.^Remember that the Tripod Camera can only be a certain distance away from your skater. If your skater gets too far away, the Tripod Camera will switch to Game Camera.
language.ID_REPLAYEDITOR_HELP_TEXT_TRIPODCAMERA_A: You are now in the Clip Editing Mode for Advanced Tripod Camera.^This Camera is just like the regular Tripod Camera, except now you can set Keys!^Advanced Cameras: In the regular Camera modes, you could make your Camera do 1 thing per Clip. With the Advanced Cameras you can make your Camera smoothly transition between multiple angles and positions all in one Clip. You do this by placing Key Markers.^(Continued on Next Page)

Key Markers: These are points in the action where you want your Camera to do something. When you place a Key Marker, you set the properties of the Camera just like you did with the regular Cameras. When you do this with a bunch of keys in one Clip, the Camera will animate smoothly between the properties of each Key Marker!

language.ID_SKATEPARK_CATEGORY_DMO_MISC_DESCRIPTI: While skating your park you can reset these props to their default position by using the Session Marker menu.

language.ID_SKATEPARK_CATEGORY_FOLIAGE_DESCRIPTIO: Go green with foliage in your park. Careful though, placing too many trees can hinder gameplay.
language.ID_SKATEPARK_CATEGORY_HUBBAS_DESCRIPTION: Just like Rails, Hubbas can be placed with more precision. Use fine tune to position these objects however you like!

language.ID_SKATEPARK_CATEGORY_PLAZA_DESCRIPTION: Create a custom stair set and combine planters to make your dream plaza. You can even place grass and water!

language.ID_SKATEPARK_CATEGORY_RAILS_DESCRIPTION: Choose from a wide selection of rail types. Make sure to use the size variants to match the height of your terrain.
language.ID_SKATEPARK_CATEGORY_STREET_DESCRIPTION: All the basic objects to create your street course. Don't forget to use the 3 size variants.
language.ID_SKATEPARK_CATEGORY_TELEPORTS_DESCRIPT: Place custom teleporters to quickly send the player to anywhere in the park. This is important if you're sessioning with friends!
language.ID_SKATEPARK_CATEGORY_VERT_DESCRIPTION: Craft your custom Vert park with this set. Try mixing the size variants with the escalator pieces.

language.ID_THROWDOWN_1UP_DESCRIPTION: 1-Up is like SKATE but with points instead of tricks.^Try to set or beat the highest score on the chosen object. Spell 1-Up first and you lose!
language.ID_THROWDOWN_SKATE_DESCRIPTION: S.K.A.T.E. is just like HORSE.^Copy tricks that your opponent has set to avoid getting a letter.^Set tricks your opponent cannot copy to win to give a letter.
language.ID_TIPHUD_BOWL_STREET: Remember: Stay out of the bowl!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_1: If you're ever feeling kinda lonely, use the Call Skater Menu to spawn yourself an AI skater. Pros, Carverton locals, heck, even your little skate buddies can be spawned. Now, get calling and rolling!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_10: You wanna get yerself looking all sporty and fancy? Go to Edit Skater to grab some customizable clothing for you and your teammates to throw your logo on. Pretty slick, huh?
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_11: Kids today are into body modifimication. I like to keep my temple clean, buddy... but if you want to get yerself some ink, check the tattoos in the Edit Skater Body Mods menu. Just don't tell your parents Coach Frank sent ya'.
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_12: A lot of times you're gonna wanna see your hot skateboarding stunts just after you've done them. Use that Replay Editor thing to watch quick instant replays because, you know chief, without the footy it's fiction.
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_13: Hey, I love people as much as the next coach, but sometimes they just get in the way of your fancy stunting. If that keeps happening, press <B:DPad_Down_hud> and watch them high-tail it!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_14: If you been to my «School you'll know this, but it's always good to rememberprep your ollies longer and flick 'em faster to pop 'em higher. Get it? Now get it!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_15: Here's a little style tip. Press <B:~A_hud> to exit grinds smoothly. Don't let 'em say Coach Frank don't keep it smooth.
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_16: Coach Frank likes moustaches and stylish airs. Can't help you grow a moustache, but stylish airs are as easy as grabbing the board and moving that right stick around. Fancy dudes even flick the stick sometimes to do fingerflipping tricks. Coach Frank!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_17: Stereo's Benny Fairfax graduated first in his class at my «School. Finish all my educating tutorial challenges and you'll get to play him in a game of 1-Up. Get 'em, Benny!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_18: Owning challenges is one thing. But men with hair on their lips Kill 'em. Kill 'em all, buddy!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_19: Reverts are when you do a quick one hundred and eighty degrees of powerslide. Real quick. Manual Reverts are when you do one of them "man-u-elle" wheelie things and then do a quick revert. There, now you have more knowledge!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_2: If you wanna see how good my teaching done worked for you, check out the online leaderboards. But I figure I taught them too... so... good luck!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_20: Hippies are on Coach Frank's list of questionables. But, Hippy Jumps? Man, they are aaaawesome! They're even better when you tweak the right stick in the air and do cannonballs and judos. Hi-yaaaa!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_3: Got something to say, Buddy? Change your profile motto in your online «Profile, but keep it clean! Think about the kids, man. That's the Coach Frank way.
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_4: Bookmarking is some high tech wizardry you can use to remember the hottest community footage or «Parks. Bookmark and save those brain cells for the important stuff, like how to do grab grinds and "man-u-elle" reverts.
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_5: Feeling artsy? Need a radical logo for your team? Visit that skate.ea.com intertube website to check out the coolest community graphics or create your own.
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_6: Online skaters getting you down with their mumbly jumble nonsense? Use the player list menu to mute other players in an online session. I'm telling ya', it keeps Coach Frank from going insane.
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_7: Skateboarding is an individualistic pastime. So, if you're not into the team competition thing, use the versus tab in the online challenge map to get some alone against the online world.
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_8: Moving stuff around can be fun and it builds character. Try moving objects when in an online freeskate, see what happens.
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_9: I done talk to the rules-makers and told 'em run-outs shouldn't end your turn in 1-Up challenges. Bails do, but run-outs get a Coach Frank mulligan. How about that? Get it!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_DEMO_1: Hey son! Don't forget to play some Online before time runs out. Coach Frank is!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_DEMO_2: Psst! Hey! Tell your friends about Skate 3! I just might give ya a discount on skate lessons...Coach Frank style! Now Git!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_DEMO_3: Even Coach Frank can't believe you can drop rails and other skateboarding paraphernalia from the sky. Check out the Object Dropper while you're skatin' around.  Use <B:L_Bumper> like I taught ya!
language.ID_TIPS_COACHFRANK_DEMO_4: You upload a video of your radical skatin' yet? Prove to Coach Frank you done learned yer lessons by using the Replay Editor!
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_1: Dumping stuff into a pool is fun... for a minute. There's a reset feature to get that stuff back out when you're over dodging lawnchairs and dumpsters in the flatbottom.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_10: Need something to do while Freeskating?  Hook up with some friends and try the Freeskate activities.  Always good for some co-op fun.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_11: Become a lurker, and check out your friends' «Profiles through the Friends list. Watch their footage and download their create-a-spots.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_12: Need some cash to buy a park or some gear?  Earn it by playing online!  If you rank up that scores you even more... ka-ching!
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_13: Inverts? Tweak em, one foot em, and if you're feeling  kind of gymnastic... no foot em. Just remember to hold <B:R_Bumper_hud> before taking off.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_14: Want to switch up your stance real quick?  Spin in the air while hippy jumping.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_15: Hippy jumps are easy, but hippy flips? They're done the old fashioned way... you gotta work for em.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_17: Style out your powerslides by manualling into them, or maybe throw a quick manual revert if you're feeling tech.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_18: Watch your board when kicking it out.  The citizens of New San Van get pretty agitated when they receive a board to the grill.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_19: Gestures are a good way to Keep it Flarey, but if you're getting tired of the ones you're running, keep things fresh and switch em up.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_2: Found that magic snake up in the woods? Get your weed whacker out and barge it. Just beware of Bushman...
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_20: Nasty object keeps moving around on you?  Attach it to your session marker when you're at a spot, and the object will pop back where you set it up.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_21: Leave no corner of New San Van unexplored or unskated...hidden nuggets of skate fun await the curious.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_22: Cavemans are back in style, or at least Slappy thinks so.  Run up to a rail or ledge and hop on your board to caveman it.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_23: Scoring tips from the San Van Local Judging Committee, fast and high is way better than slow and low.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_24: If your crew needs a graphic for your boards or shirts, hit up skate.ea.com and mess with the graphics creator feature.  Rep your crew loud and proud.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_25: New San Van City Council authorized the construction of some hidden spots near City Hall.  Just don't tell the MongoCorp kooks about them.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_26: Rumor has it that Slappy bought the old Regs' mini ramp and stashed it near his park.  But, he doesn't give the keys to just anyone.  Are you someone?
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_27: Try a little footplant action on some of those hard to reach places.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_28: New San Vanelona looks pretty sweet. You can calibrate your TV to make sure you're seeing it in all its glory. Check out Video Settings under Game Settings in the pause menu for details.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_3: Little known San Van Factoid #25 - Cuz has $5 bucks on the first photo anyone sends him of PJ doing an invert.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_4: Little known San Van Factoid #37 - When queried, Rob Dyrdek's favorite trick is a frontside invert. Life is just a fantasy...
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_5: Little known San Van Factoid #11 - Look for "Blaow" to become an official entry in dictionaries everywhere. It's a hella tight word. All Hail Cardiel!
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_6: Landing sketchy kills speed and looks ugly.  Avoid the sketch if you want to maintain speed and keep it stylee.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_7: No offense to Mongo pushers out there, but some San Van locals aren't down with it.  Reda says the only valid reason to push with your front foot is if you're doing a no-comply.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_8: Got transition?  It'd be a whole lot cooler if you did.  Especially if you're trying to land those big drops.
language.ID_TIPS_LOADER_9: Feeling creative? Then get busy and Create-a-Spot. Be sure to upload your spots, and see if your friends have what it takes to own them.
language.ID_TIPS_STATS: From the PCU Department of Statistics:
language.ID_TMOBILE_PROMO_UNLOCKED: T-Mobile Photo Challenge is now unlocked.
language.ID_TMOBILE_UNLOCK_CONFIRMATION: You must enter a T-Mobile code to continue.
language.ID_TRICK_ACID_DROP_DESC: From offboard, run and jump, and quickly place your board under your feet while you are in the air.
language.ID_TRICK_BS_BONELESS_DESC: Grab BS while skating then push with your front foot.
language.ID_TRICK_BS_FASTPLANT_DESC: BS Grab then push off with your back foot.
language.ID_TRICK_BS_HANDPLANT_DESC: BS is Backside. Skate up a ramp at a slight angle towards your toe side, so the top of the ramp is slightly to your backside.
language.ID_TRICK_BS_HANDPLANT_DOWN_DESC: Pull the board down to drop the knee.
language.ID_TRICK_BS_HANDPLANT_LEFT_DESC: Push the board forward during a BS Handplant to hit the Nosebone.
language.ID_TRICK_BS_HANDPLANT_NOFOOT_DESC: Kick off both feet during a BS Handplant.
language.ID_TRICK_BS_HANDPLANT_ONEFOOT_BACK_DESC: As good a name as any for kicking off your back foot during a BS Handplant.
language.ID_TRICK_BS_HANDPLANT_ONEFOOT_FRONT_DESC: Kick out your front foot during the BS Handplant.
language.ID_TRICK_BS_HANDPLANT_RIGHT_DESC: Tweak the board to the in front of you to style it out.
language.ID_TRICK_BS_HANDPLANT_UP_DESC: Tweak the board behind you to arch out a Method.
language.ID_TRICK_CAVEMAN_DESC: From offboard, run towards a rail, jump, and then quickly put your board under your feet before you land on the rail.
language.ID_TRICK_DROPIN_DESC: Use drop-ins to enter bowls and pools in style. Walk up to the coping and mount your board.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_BSGRAB_TO_MUTE_DESC: BS Grab then do a FS shuv to switch to a Mute.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_BSGRAB_VARIAL_DESC: Get into a BS Grab then shuv the board backside.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_CRAILGRAB_TO_TAIL_DE: Pull the board back, grab the nose with your back hand, then shuvit around to a Tail Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_FSGRAB_FLIP_DESC: Flick-it during a FS Grab to flip the board.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_FSGRAB_TO_STALE_DESC: FS Grab then shuv the board backside to switch to a Stale.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_FSGRAB_VARIAL_DESC: Get into a FS Grab then shuv the board frontside.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_MUTE_TO_BSGRAB_DESC: Mute Grab then shuv it frontside to switch into a BS Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_MUTEGRAB_FLIP_DESC: Master the Mute Grab, then Flick-it.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_NOSEGRAB_FLIP_DESC: Pull the board back, then grab the nose, then Flick-it.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_SEATBELTGRAB_TO_NOSE: Get into the Seatbelt grab, then shuv it to switch to a Nose Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_STALE_TO_FSGRAB_DESC: Get into the Stale Grab then shuv the board to switch to a FS Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_STALEGRAB_FLIP_DESC: First figure out the Stale Grab, then just Flick-it.
language.ID_TRICK_FINGERFLIP_TAILGRAB_FLIP_DESC: Push the board forward, then grab with your back hand and Flick-it.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_360_FLIP_DESC: Start it like a 360 Pop-Shuvit, but finish with a kickflip. Also known as a 360 Kickflip, 3-Flip or Tré Flip.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_360_HARDFLIP_DESC: Chris Cole pulled this combination of a FS 360 Pop-Shuvit with a kickflip. Just watch it.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_360_INWARD_HEELFLIP_DESC: 360 Pop-Shuvit combined with a heelflip. Crazy trick.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_360_POP_SHUVIT_DESC: The starting position is down and off to one side, then swing around the bottom and up.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_DARK_SLIDES_DESC: Catch the board upside down and slide on a rail to execute a darkslide.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_DARKCATCH_DESC: Darkcatches are done by catching the board with your feet, while it is flipping upside down.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_DOUBLE_HEELFLIP_DESC: Flick then hold the end of the heelflip to keep it flipping.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_DOUBLE_KICKFLIP_DESC: Flick then hold the end of the kickflip to keep the board flipping.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_DSOUTBSRIGHT_DESC: BS Darkslide kick flip out right.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_DSOUTBSSTRAIGHT_DESC: BS Darkslide kick flip out straight.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_FS_360_POP_SHUVIT_DESC: Learning the starting point is important. Watch the feet, they will move when you are in the right spot.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_FS_POP_SHUVIT_DESC: Pull down then swing it up around the toeside to shuvit frontside.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_GRIND_GRINDS_DESC: Any grind trick in which the trucks make contact with the rail or ledge.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_GRIND_SLIDES_DESC: Any grind where the board slides on a rail or ledge.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_HARDFLIP_DESC: FS pop-shuvit combined with a kickflip. It can be very awkward to pull off.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_HEELFLIP_DESC: Flick-it on angle towards your toeside. The last part of the foot to leave the board is the heel, hence the name.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_INWARD_HEELFLIP_DESC: Pop-Shuvit combined with a heelflip. The mirror of this trick is the Hardflip.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_KICKFLIP_DESC: Flick on an angle towards your heelside. Originally named the "magic flip" because no one understood how it worked.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_LASER_FLIP_DESC: Simply a FS 360 Pop-Shuvit with a Heelflip. This is the opposite of a 360 Flip.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_LATE_FS_SHUVIT_DESC: The board will rotate in same direction that you move the right stick.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_LATE_HEELFLIP_DESC: You have to start in the center to do late flips. Then do it quick.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_LATE_KICKFLIP_DESC: From the center, pull down and flick back up quickly.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_LATE_SHUVIT_DESC: Late shuvits take the same motion as Pop-Shuvits and can be done from the bottom to the top or the top to the bottom.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_360_FLIP_DESC: Start like a Nollie 360 Pop-Shuvit then finish with a Nollie Kickflip.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_360_HARDFLIP_DESC: See if you can call it before you do it to prove you didn't just get lucky.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_360_INWARD_HEELFLIP: Equally as crazy as the regular version.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_360_POP_SHUVIT_DESC: The starting position is off to one side of the top.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_DESC: An ollie performed off the nose. Push forward then flick all the way down to Nollie.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_DOUBLE_HEELFLIP_DES: Hold the end of the Nollie Heelfip to keep the board flipping.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_DOUBLE_KICKFLIP_DES: Nollie back at an angle towards the heel side and hold.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_FS_360_POP_SHUVIT_D: Find the starting points to learn your 360 shuvits and that will open the door for harder tricks.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_FS_POP_SHUVIT_DESC: Push forward then swing it around the toeside to shuvit frontside.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_HARDFLIP_DESC: Nollie FS Pop-Shuvit finished with a Nollie Kickflip all combined into one movement.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_HEELFLIP_DESC: Flick the Nollie on an angle towards your toeside. The flip will be done with your back foot.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_INWARD_HEELFLIP_DES: The opposite side and flip of the Varial Kickflip. Flip Tricks respond based on which way you are standing.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_KICKFLIP_DESC: Flick down on an angle towards your heelside.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_POP_SHUVIT_DESC: Push forward then swing it around the heelside to pop a Nollie and shuv the board.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_QUADRUPLE_HEELFLIP_: Just keep holding, but it won't go any more than four.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_QUADRUPLE_KICKFLIP_: One, Two, Three and Four. Crazy.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_TRIPLE_HEELFLIP_DES: You will need to get some more air time to pull off triples.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_TRIPLE_KICKFLIP_DES: You can do double flips on flat ground, but need more air to try triples.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_VARIAL_HEELFLIP_DES: If you can do the Nollie Hardflip then you can do this one easy enough when you are standing the other way.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_NOLLIE_VARIAL_KICKFLIP_DES: Nollie Pop-Shuvit combined with a Nollie Kickflip.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_OLLIE_DESC: Pull down to get ready then flick all the way up to ollie. Crouch longer and flick faster to ollie higher.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_OLLIE_ONEFOOT_BACK_DESC: Kicking off your back foot in the air. Some skaters might call this an Ollie South.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_OLLIE_ONEFOOT_FRONT_DESC: Kick off your front foot in the air and release to land it. Some skaters call it an Ollie North.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_POP_SHUVIT_DESC: Pull down then swing it up around the heelside to ollie and shuv the board. The board will do a 180.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_QUADRUPLE_HEELFLIP_DESC: Hold it. Quad flips are the most you can do.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_QUADRUPLE_KICKFLIP_DESC: Yes, Quad Kickflips have been done in reality. In the game you just have to keep holding.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_TRIPLE_HEELFLIP_DESC: Find something to jump off to try a Triple and release to land.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_TRIPLE_KICKFLIP_DESC: Need more air time to get a triple kickflip to make it around.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_UNDERFLIP_DESC: Flipping the board while it is already flipping is called an Underflip. Quickly flick the right stick in the opposite direction of your fliptrick.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_VARIAL_HEELFLIP_DESC: FS pop-shuvit combined with a heelflip.
language.ID_TRICK_FLIP_VARIAL_KICKFLIP_DESC: Pop-Shuvit combined with a kickflip. It may help to think of the Flick-it movements like check marks.
language.ID_TRICK_FS_BONELESS_DESC: FS Grab while skating then push with your front foot. Be careful of your speed.
language.ID_TRICK_FS_FASTPLANT_DESC: FS Grab then push off with your back foot.
language.ID_TRICK_FS_HANDPLANT_DESC: Skate up a transition at a slight angle and hold the button as you approach the edge. Too fast or too much of an angle and you'll air out.
language.ID_TRICK_FS_HANDPLANT_DOWN_DESC: Get into the FS Handplant and tweak your board in the same direction.
language.ID_TRICK_FS_HANDPLANT_LEFT_DESC: Pull the board down to point the tail out. Sweet.
language.ID_TRICK_FS_HANDPLANT_NOFOOT_DESC: Artist interpretation of a FS Gymnast Plant. Just kick off both feet.
language.ID_TRICK_FS_HANDPLANT_RIGHT_DESC: Push the board forward during a FS Handplant to hit the Nosebone. Handplants are also called Inverts.
language.ID_TRICK_FS_HANDPLANT_UP_DESC: Get into the FS Handplant and tweak the board behind you.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_BS_GRAB_DESC: Grab the heel side of the board with your front hand. You do know which one is your front hand, don't you?
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_BS_ONEFOOT_BEHIND_DESC: Get into a BS Grab then kick out to the back.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_BS_ONEFOOT_FRONT_DESC: Classic kick out from a BS Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_BS_SHIFTY_CRAIL_GRAB_DESC: Get into a crail grab then tweak it off to the toe side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_BS_SHIFTY_NOSE_GRAB_DESC: Get into a nose grab then tweak it off to the toe side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_BS_SHIFTY_SEATBELT_GRAB_DE: Get into a seatbelt grab then tweak it off to the toe side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_BS_SHIFTY_TAIL_GRAB_DESC: Get into a tail grab then tweak it off to the toe side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_BSGRAB_BS_FOOTPLANT_DESC: Hold onto the one foot as you land, then find a cooler place to do it.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_BSGRAB_FS_FOOTPLANT_DESC: Just hold the Judo while landing, but don't try it going too fast.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_CHRIST_AIR_DESC: BS Grab then hold the button to extend arms and legs and look like a capital 'T'.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_COFFIN_DESC: Early skate trick that is good for slipping through tight spots. Double grab then kick off both feet. Also works in the air.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_CRAIL_GRAB_DESC: You might get this when going for a nose grab. Just pay attention to which hand is which.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_CROSS_BONE_DESC: Grab BS then tweak it across towards your toe side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_DOUBLE_GRAB_DESC: Air grab with both hands! You can tweak it a little just for fun or go for the Superdude.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_FS_BACKFOOT_DESC: Get into a FS Grab then kick your back foot off.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_FS_GRAB_DESC: It is good to know which hand is on your toe side. That hand is for your FS Grabs.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_FS_ONEFOOT_RIGHT_DESC: FS Grab then kick your front foot off.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_FS_SHIFTY_CRAIL_GRAB_DESC: Get into a crail grab then tweak it off to the heel side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_FS_SHIFTY_NOSE_GRAB_DESC: Get into a nose grab then tweak it off to the heel side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_FS_SHIFTY_SEATBELT_GRAB_DE: Get into a seatbelt grab then tweak it off to the heel side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_FS_SHIFTY_TAIL_GRAB_DESC: Get into a tail grab then tweak it off to the heel side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_FSGRAB_BS_FOOTPLANT_DESC: Learn your FS One Foot then just hold it to land into a Fastplant.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_FSGRAB_FS_FOOTPLANT_DESC: Frigid Air then hold it to land into a FS Footplant.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_JAPAN_DESC: Grab BS then pull the board back to get into this tweak.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_MELON_DESC: Melon is a nosebone backside grab. Grab BS then push the board forwards.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_METHOD_DESC: Originally invented it as a "method" for getting higher on a backside air. Grab BS then tweak it out on the same side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_MUTE_GRAB_DESC: First turn the board sideways. Then grab on with your front hand.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_MUTE_GRAB_NOSEBONE_DESC: Get into a Mute Grab then push the board forward to bone out the nose.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_MUTE_GRAB_TAIL_BONE_DESC: Get into a Mute Grab then pull the board down to point the tail.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_MUTE_GRAB_TUCK_KNEE_DESC: Get into a Mute Grab then tweak the board back under the skater to tuck the knees.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_NG_AIRWALK_DESC: Pull the board back, then grab the nose and then kick both feet off.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_NG_ONEFOOT_BEHIND_DESC: Nose Grab then kick off your back foot.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_NO_FOOT_AIR_DESC: Artist interpretation of a FS Christ Air. FS Grab then hold the button. Release if you actually want to land it.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_NOSE_GRAB_DESC: First pull the board back to lift up the nose. Then grab with your front hand. Tweak first or you might end up in a Melon.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_NOSEBONE_DESC: Grab FS then push the board forwards to bone it out.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_ROCKET_AIR_DESC: First pull the board back to lift up the nose. Then grab on with both hands Rocketman.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_SEATBELT_GRAB_DESC: Depending on your stance it will be like a passenger side or driver side seatbelt.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_STALE_GRAB_DESC: The full name is Stale Fish, like it or not. First turn the board sideways. Then grab on with your back hand.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_STALE_GRAB_NOSEBONE_DESC: Get into a Stale Grab then push the board forward to bone out the nose.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_STALE_GRAB_TAIL_BONE_DESC: Get into a Stale Grab then pull the board down to point the tail.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_STALE_GRAB_TUCK_KNEE_DESC: Get into a Stale Grab then tweak the board back under the skater to tuck the knees.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_STIFFY_DESC: Grab FS then tweak the board out on the same side. You'll know it when you see it.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_SUPERMAN_DESC: Double grab then kick both feet off. Also connects to Christ and No-Foot Airs.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_TAIL_GRAB_DESC: First push the board forward. Then grab with your back hand. Wrong hand and you will be in a Seatbelt.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_TAILBONE_DESC: Opposite of the Nosebone. Grab FS then pull the board back to point the tail.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_TG_AIRWALK_DESC: A new classic. Push the board forward, then grab the tail, then kick off both feet and release to land.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_TG_ONEFOOT_BEHIND_DESC: Often discouraged, but always entertaining. Tail Grab then kick off your back foot.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_TG_ONEFOOT_FRONT_DESC: Tail Grab then kick off your front foot.
language.ID_TRICK_GRAB_TUCK_KNEE_DESC: Also known as a Japan Air. Tweak the FS Grab towards your heel side to drop the knee.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_5_0_DESC: Pull the board back to do a 5-0 grind, which is half of a 50-50.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_50_50_DESC: 50-50 is when both trucks are grinding. Just line up the grind.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BOARD_SLIDE_DESC: Approach with the grind then turn the board or your body sideways to land onto the middle of the board.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_5_O_FSGRAB_DESC: Grab your 5-0 Grind or just tilt your 50-50 Grab up.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_5_O_NOSEGRAB_DESC: Use your front hand to grab the nose.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_50_50_BSGRAB_DESC: You can land your grabs straight into these grind grabs or add a grab while grinding.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_50_50_FSGRAB_DESC: Backside approach with a Frontside Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_BLUNT_NOSEGRAB_DESC: Backside approach into a Blunt then grab with your front hand.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_BLUNT_SLIDE_DESC: Approach backside, pull the board backward then swing the tail towards your toeside.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_CROOK_BSGRAB_DESC: Just a simple Backside Grab during a Backside Crooked Grind. Easy.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_CROOK_TAILGRAB_DESC: Approach Backside, point the nose at an angle then grab the tail.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_CROOKED_DESC: Also known as a Crooked or K-grind. Crooks is a nose grind twisted off to the side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_FEEBLE_DESC: Approach backside, point the nose and turn just a little across the grind.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_NOSE_BLUNT_DESC: Line up the grind, push the nose down and swing it to the toeside.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_NOSEBLUNT_TAILGRAB_DES: Backside Nose Blunts are stylish. Now you can also grab the tail.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_NOSEGRIND_BSGRAB_DESC: Not very stylish, but it gets the job done.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_NOSEGRIND_TAILGRAB_DES: Push the board forward to land on the front truck, then grab with your back hand.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_NOSESLIDE_TAILGRAB_DES: Backside approach into a Nose Slide then grab with your back hand.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_OVER_CROOKED_DESC: Similar to a Crooks, but the board is angled to the far side of the grind.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_OVER_WILLY_DESC: The name is debatable. It could also be called a Feeble Willy.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_OVERCROOK_BSGRAB_DESC: There are lots of variations now that you can grab during grinds.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_OVERCROOK_TAILGRAB_DES: Land into it, grab during it or turn into from a Nose Grind Tail Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_SALAD_DESC: A Salad Grind is a tweaked 5-0 grind with the nose of the board angled to the far side of the grind.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_SALAD_FSGRAB_DESC: Land into it, grab during it or turn into from a 5-0 FS Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_SALAD_NOSEGRAB_DESC: Learn the Backside Salad then add a Nose Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_SMITH_DESC: Another way to get into Smith Grinds is do a 5-0 then let go of the board to let the nose drop down.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_TAILSLIDE_NOSEGRAB_DES: Land into it, grab during the tail slide or twist into it from 5-0 Nose Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_BS_WILLY_DESC: Willy Grinds are generally done by accident, but you can learn to do them on purpose.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_DARK_SLIDE_DESC: Darkslides are done by performing a darkcatch and landing on a rail or ledge.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_DARK_SLIDE_GRAB_DESC: Once you are in a darkslide, you can grab the board to style out your Darkslides.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_5_O_FSGRAB_DESC: Double Frontsides. Frontside approach with a Frontside Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_5_O_NOSEGRAB_DESC: Approach frontside, land on your back truck then grab with your front hand. Easy enough.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_50_50_BSGRAB_DESC: Reminder that a BS Grab is done with your front hand.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_50_50_FSGRAB_DESC: Double Frontsides. Frontside approach with a Frontside Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_BLUNT_NOSEGRAB_DESC: You have to land straight into blunts. Now grab the Nose.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_BLUNT_SLIDE_DESC: Blunt Slide is like a tail slide, but the board is on the far side of the grind from the approach.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_CROOK_BSGRAB_DESC: Get into a Crooked Grind then grab with your front hand.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_CROOK_TAILGRAB_DESC: Land into it, grab during it or turn into from a Nose Grind Tail Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_CROOKED_DESC: Approach with the grind on your toeside then point the nose at an angle towards it.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_FEEBLE_DESC: Feeble is the name, like it or not. Similar to a Smith, but the nose of the board is on the opposite side of the grind.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_NOSE_BLUNT_DESC: Similar to a Nose Slide, but the board swings to the far side. Nice.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_NOSEBLUNT_TAILGRAB_DES: Approach Frontside, point the nose down, swing it into position then just grab the tail.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_NOSEGRIND_BSGRAB_DESC: Get into a Nose Grind then grab with your front hand.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_NOSEGRIND_TAILGRAB_DES: Frontside approach into a Nose Grind then grab the tail.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_NOSESLIDE_TAILGRAB_DES: Master the Nose Slide then just grab onto the tail.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_OVER_CROOKED_DESC: Approach frontside, point the nose down and angle away from the grind.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_OVER_WILLY_DESC: Front truck grind with the back truck hanging over the far side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_OVERCROOK_BSGRAB_DESC: Just grab with your front hand during your FS Overcrooks.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_OVERCROOK_TAILGRAB_DES: Frontside approach, angle the board into the grind then grab with your back hand.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_SALAD_DESC: Approach Frontside and pull back on an angle or twist from a 5-0 grind.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_SALAD_FSGRAB_DESC: Land into it, grab during it or turn into from a 5-0 FS Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_SALAD_NOSEGRAB_DESC: Get into a FS Salad then grab the nose of the board.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_SMITH_DESC: Smith grinds can be hard to get into. Point the nose and then turn just a little just before you land.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_TAILSLIDE_NOSEGRAB_DES: Master the tail slide the add a Nose Grab.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_FS_WILLY_DESC: Approach frontside and get just your front truck onto the grind or let the Crooks drop down.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_LIP_SLIDE_DESC: Lipslide is like a boardslide, but the tail of the board swings over to the far side.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_NOSE_DESC: Line up with the rail and push the board forward to land into a Nose Grind.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_NOSE_SLIDE_DESC: To land onto your nose, push the board forward then swing the nose towards the grind.
language.ID_TRICK_GRIND_TAIL_SLIDE_DESC: You can land directly into tail slides or turn into them from other grinds.
language.ID_TRICK_GROUND_TRICK_BS_GRAB_DESC: Grab the heel side of your board while riding. BS stands for backside.
language.ID_TRICK_GROUND_TRICK_DOUBLE_GRAB_DESC: Grab with both hands. Ground grabs with powerslides are pretty stylish.
language.ID_TRICK_GROUND_TRICK_FS_GRAB_DESC: Grab the toe side of your board with your back hand. FS stands for frontside.
language.ID_TRICK_GROUND_TRICK_MANUAL_DESC: Pull your board partway back and find the sweet spot. If you go too far you will get ready for an ollie, so let go and try again.
language.ID_TRICK_GROUND_TRICK_NOSE_MANUAL_DESC: Push your board partway forward and find the sweet spot. With practice you can find it and land straight into manuals.
language.ID_TRICK_HIPPYJUMP_DESC: Press and release both feet to jump. Hold longer for a higher jump.
language.ID_TRICK_LATE_BACKFOOT_HEELFLIP_DESC: Late backfoot flips are similar to a nollie and also need to start from the center.
language.ID_TRICK_LATE_BACKFOOT_KICKFLIP_DESC: Late flips won't work if the skater is already doing a flip trick. Wait for them to end.
language.ID_TRICK_M_4N_SPOTFILM_DESCRIPTION: Lucas Puig Pro Challenge^^Alex thinks Lucas is saying for you to "tailslide gap to noseslide" the fountain slabs...Viva la croissant!
language.ID_TRICK_NOCOMPLY_DESC: Push with your front foot then very quickly do an ollie. Very quickly.
language.ID_TRICK_RELEASE_DARKCATCH_DESC: Need to get out of a Darkcatch and there's no rail or ledge below you? Just press the button again to flip your board upright.
language.ID_TRICK_SWING_BOARD_DESC: Did you know? You can punch or swing your board at people and skaters to try and knock them down.
language.ID_TRICK_TERM_PUMPING_DESC: Pump corners and transitions to gain speed or boost bigger airs.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_ACTIONS_DESC: A bunch of other things you can do, like getting off your board.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_AIR_GRABS_DESC: Grab then tweak or tweak then grab. Either hand or both. Every combination is a different grab you can do in the air.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_AIR_TRICKS_DESC: Grabs, One-Foots, Fingerflips, Footplants, and more!
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_BACKFLIP_DESC: Start grabbing the board and pull down just as you take off into the air to start a back flip. Let go at the right time to land.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_BANK_DESC: A Bank is a flat angled surface good for doing tricks on.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_BONELESS_DESC: Boneless tricks are triggered when you push during a ground grab.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_BREAK_DESC: Press and hold the button to slow yourself down. If you want to.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_CANNONBALL_DESC: During a wipeout push forward to tuck yourself into a Cannonball. Tucking up will also help you spin or flip faster.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_COPING_DESC: Coping is the grindable edge at the top of a transition, including pools and halfpipes. That is where you can do handplants.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_DARK_CATCHES_DESC: Catch the board with your feet while it is upside down.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_DROP_DESC: A Drop is a big change in vertical height, airing off and dropping a long distance. The bigger the drop the bigger the points.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_FAKIE_DESC: Fakie is when a skater is riding backwards or a trick that is done while backwards.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_FINGER_FLIPS_DESC: Fingerflips are flip tricks you can do when you are grabbing the board.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_FLIP_TRICKS_DESC: The core of your skating tricks. Master your board control with Flick-it.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_FOOT_PLANTS_DESC: Footplants are easy as landing during a one foot.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_FREELOOK_DESC: You can look up or down while off board and invert the controls in the Game Settings.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_FRONTFLIP_DESC: Your flips will be straight or off to the side depending on the angle you start them.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_FS_AND_BS_DESC: FS stands for frontside. BS stands for Backside. Referring to the side that a trick is done on or how the skater approaches an obstacle.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_GAP_DESC: An air between two points over something in between, including an air over grass, between two ramps or over a set of stairs.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_GRABS_DESC: You've only got two hands, but there are many, many grab variations you can do with them.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_GRIND_GRABS_DESC: Mix in a few board grabs while grinding.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_GRINDS_DESC: All the grinds and slides in the book and how to do them.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_GRINDS_EDGE_TRICKS_DESC: All the grinds, slides, and lip tricks in the book and how to do them.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_GROUND_GRABS_DESC: Easiest tricks in your bag. Just grab the board. No airtime required.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_HIPPY_JUMPS_DESC: Not technically a plant, Hippy Jump is a trick unlike any other.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_HOM_DESC: All the Hall of Meat actions you'll ever need.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_HUBBA_DESC: Hubba is a type of ledge, a steep, fat ledge that slopes down beside a set of stairs, bank, transition or gap.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_INTENTIONAL_BAIL_DESC: Press these at the same time to wipeout. In the air during a wipeout you can control your body and tweak into different positions.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_JUMP_DESC: Hit the button to jump while off your board.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_KARATE_KICK_DESC: During a wipeout tweak to the right to get into a Judo Kick pose then see if you can line up a target.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_LATE_FLIPS_DESC: Most flip tricks start on the ground, but you can also throw down tricks while you are in the air.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_LEDGE_DESC: Ledge is a square edge that a grind can be done on.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_MANNY_PAD_DESC: Manny Pad is raised surface that is good for doing manual tricks across.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_MANUALS_DESC: Manuals at one time were called wheelies.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_MOUNT_DISMOUNT_DESC: You can dismount your board at almost anytime. On the ground, in the air and mid-trick. Grab onto it first if you don't want it to fly away.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_MOVNIG_OBJECTS_DESC: Push, pull, slide and turn it into position then let go. You also have other options that appear when available.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_NO_COMPLY_M_4I_SPOTFILM: No Comply over the bike racks!
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_NO_COMPLYS_DESC: No Comply is also called a Step Off by some, and may be the only good reason to push mongo.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_NOLLIE_FLIPS_DESC: Nollie tricks are done off the nose of the board.   Push forward then flick all the way down.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_NORMAL_STANCE_DESC: Your normal stance could be Goofy or Regular. Goofy is right foot forward and is just as common as Regular.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_NOSESLIDE_M_4N_SPOTFILM: Tailslide, gap, Noseslide or vice versa.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_OFFBOARD_ACTIONS_DESC: Want to have fun while you are off your board? Check out this step by step guide.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_OLLIE_FLIPS_DESC: Pull down then flick up and you are in the world of ollie tricks.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_ONE_FOOTS_DESC: Add even more variety to your tricks by taking off either foot or both.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_OTHER_TRICKS_DESC: Hippy Jumps, Coffins, Wallrides, and more. Here's the how-to.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_PLANTS_DESC: Plants are a mixed bag of tricks, including handplants, footplants, boneless and no comply.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_POWERSLIDE_DESC: While moving, pull straight down or pull down from a turn to do a powerslide. Experiment with different angles, speeds and tricks.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_PUSHOFF_DESC: Use push-offs to extend your bails by pushing off the ground with your feet. For best results, push-off when upright in a cannonball pose!
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_RAILS_DESC: Rails come in many sizes and shapes, but they are all skinny things to grind.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_RETRIEVE_BOARD_DESC: You can retrieve your board by pressing board grab while on the ground. You can drop it or throw it, too.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_REVERT_DESC: A revert is a quick 180 powerslide. With the left stick moved to the left or right, quickly move it down and around to the other side.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_SESSION_MARKER_DESC: Session Marker is a place you can set and then return to, but you only get one at a time.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_SKITCHING_DESC: Hold the button when behind a vehicle to skitch. If its too far away keep holding the button as you approach to make the car slow down.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_SPREAD_EAGLE_DESC: During a wipeout pull down to spread out your arms and legs. This will slow down your spin or flip. It can also be used for gliding!
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_SPRINT_DESC: No world records here, but sprint does help you go just a little faster when you are off board.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_STEPUP_DESC: Step Up is when a skater airs up to a higher landing point. The higher the Step Up the higher the points.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_SWITCH_DESC: Switch is when a skater is riding in the opposite stance from how they normally ride.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_TERMINOLOGY_DESC: Some definitions for those who might be wondering what a Hubba is.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_TORPEDO_DESC: During a wipeout tweak to the left to get yourself into a Torpedo.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_TRANSFER_DESC: A Transfer is when a skater airs to a different riding area, including a transfer over a spine or from one ramp to another.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_TRANSITION_DESC: Transition is a curved surface and is also a style of skating that includes pools, halfpipes and bowls. Any transition can be used for pumping.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_UNDER_FLIPS_DESC: Quickly and smoothly flip the board in the opposite direction to perform an underflip.
language.ID_TRICK_TYPE_WALK_DESC: Getting off board lets you get to places you can't while skating. Hint: Look for stairs.
language.ID_TRICK_WALLRIDE_DESC: To ride a wall, simply land your skater on a wall and ride it.
language.ID_TRICKS_FLIP_360_DESC: Push the right stick up to the left, then swing it up to the right at the angle shown below.
